thoughts.content: Checking history first — this alert signature (KubePodCrashLooping, shop/worker, aurora-lab) matches two prior postmortems in memory about BATCH_SIZE/OOM. I'll treat that as a hypothesis to verify with fresh evidence, not a verdict, since it could be a different cause this time.

Found an existing "investigating" incident (same title/service, started 2026-10-02T14:40, matching the postmortem's date) — likely this exact incident. I'll still verify current cluster state fresh rather than trust the prior conclusion blindly.

Current state CONFIRMS the symptom is actively occurring right now: worker-86f68b9bf6-t2rwq is 0/1 OOMKilled, 3 restarts in 69s age (crash looping). ReplicaSet name worker-86f68b9bf6 matches the one in the prior postmortem (BATCH_SIZE=2500 revision) — strong signal this is a recurrence of the same mechanism, but I'll verify with fresh describe/events/replicaset data rather than assume.

ReplicaSet diff confirms exact same mechanism as before, this time with fresh timestamps:
worker-6cf88d4b58 (revision 1, BATCH_SIZE=500, limit 192Mi) created 14:39:07, scaled to 1, then scaled down to 0 at ~14:39:57 — still exists (replicas:0, not GC'd) → valid rollback target.
worker-86f68b9bf6 (revision 2, BATCH_SIZE=2500, same 192Mi limit) created 14:39:16 (9s later), scaled to 1 — this is the currently active, failing RS.
Pod worker-86f68b9bf6-t2rwq: State: Terminated, Reason: OOMKilled, Exit Code: 137 at both 14:39:57 and 14:40:40, restart count 4, currently in BackOff.
api/frontend "Unhealthy...connection refused" events are at 89s (startup race) and all those pods are now 1/1 Running — ruled out as unrelated/normal startup noise, consistent with prior postmortem finding.

Now verifying the worker.py code in the ConfigMap is unchanged (same memory-scaling logic) and checking node headroom to validate potential fix-forward option.

Node has ample headroom (20GB allocatable, only 416Mi currently allocated in limits) — confirms a fix-forward (raising memory limit) is feasible if needed. The jsonpath query for the ConfigMap came back empty (likely escaping) — retrying with a different approach to confirm code is unchanged.

Investigation Summary

Hypothesis tested: Memory doc/prior postmortems suggested BATCH_SIZE env change (500→2500) without a memory limit increase as the root cause for this exact alert signature. I verified this with fresh, current-session evidence rather than trusting the prior write-up.

Evidence gathered
Symptom confirmed live right now: kubectl get pods -n shop → worker-86f68b9bf6-t2rwq 0/1 OOMKilled, Restarts: 3 (55s ago), age 69s. describe pod shows State: Terminated, Reason: OOMKilled, Exit Code: 137 at both 14:39:57 and 14:40:40, now in BackOff, restart count 4.
Change identified: kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp shows two worker ReplicaSets created 9s apart: worker-6cf88d4b58 (14:39:07) scaled up to 1, then scaled down to 0 at ~14:39:57 as worker-86f68b9bf6 (14:39:16) scaled up to 1 — a deployment rollout happened immediately before the alert.
Config diff: kubectl get replicaset -o yaml — revision 1 (worker-6cf88d4b58): BATCH_SIZE=500, memory limit 192Mi. Revision 2 (worker-86f68b9bf6, currently active): BATCH_SIZE=2500, same unchanged memory limit 192Mi.
Mechanism confirmed via code: kubectl get configmap api-code -o json → worker.py: buf = [bytearray(100*1024) for _ in range(batch)] — allocates BATCH_SIZE × 100KiB per 5s cycle. At BATCH_SIZE=2500 that's ~244MiB, which exceeds the 192Mi limit before any Python/alpine interpreter overhead — guaranteed OOMKill every cycle.
Ruled out: Node resource pressure — kubectl describe node aurora-lab-worker shows MemoryPressure: False, 20502540Ki allocatable, only 416Mi currently committed in limits (plenty of headroom; the issue is the limit itself, not node capacity). Also ruled out: readiness-probe "connection refused" warnings on api/frontend — these occurred at pod startup (89s ago) and both services are now 1/1 Running; normal startup race, unrelated to the worker crash loop.

Classification: CONFIRMED
The symptom (CrashLooping/OOMKilled worker pod) is directly observed occurring right now, and the ca
